why: The answer says StdDraw.point(256, 256) is drawn in pixels at the middle of the default window, which is the documented PixelCoordinates misconception: the default scale is the unit square, so (256, 256) lies far outside the window and only the square shows.

concepts.quote: The square uses 0.5 as the centre
concepts.why: It correctly says the square is centred on (0.5, 0.5) but says nothing about its size (side 0.5) or the rest of the call.
The answer makes no claim about double.

concepts.quote: the point uses pixels, so both are in the middle
concepts.why: This is the PixelCoordinates wrong rule: the default coordinates are the unit square, not pixels, so the point is off the canvas.
Without setXscale or setYscale the scale stays the unit square, so (256, 256) is not the centre.
